title: Belitong Geopark Run 2027 Review: A Fourth Leg on the Tin and Pepper Island
meta_description: Belitong Geopark Run 2027 review: April 18, part of the Geopark Run Series -- a fourth leg on Belitung, joining Ijen, Minang and Ciletuh legs.
dek: Set for 18 April 2027, this is the fourth leg of the official Geopark Run Series, extending the same organisation covered at Ijen, Minang and Ciletuh elsewhere in this research to Belitung -- Indonesia's tin and pepper island.
verdict: Belitong Geopark Run is the fourth confirmed leg of the Geopark Run Series covered extensively in this research batch -- Ijen's volcanic highlands, Minang's canyon country, Ciletuh's UNESCO-recognised coastline, and now Belitung, historically known for tin mining and pepper. That consistent multi-leg expansion across genuinely different Indonesian landscapes signals a maturing, well-organised national series. Three distances (5K/10K/21.1K) keep it in line with the series format. Venue details and registration remain 'coming soon' at the time of this research.

sections.heading: The Series' Fourth Confirmed Leg
paragraphs: Belitong Geopark Run offers three distances -- 5K, 10K and 21.1K -- on Pulau Belitung (also spelled Belitong), in Kepulauan Bangka Belitung province. [1] This research batch has now covered four legs of the same Geopark Run Series: the debut Ijen Geopark Run in East Java's volcanic highlands, the Minang Geopark Run through West Sumatra's canyon country, the UNESCO-recognised Ciletuh Geopark Run in West Java, and now this Belitung leg -- a genuinely broad, multi-island national expansion.

sections.heading: Belitung: Tin, Pepper, and a Distinct Culture
paragraphs: Belitung is a 4,859 sq km island off Sumatra's east coast in the Java Sea, historically known for its tin mining and pepper production, with a 2020 census population of 309,097. [2] The island's population blends ethnic Malay speakers of a distinct local dialect with Chinese Hokkien and Hakka communities -- similar cultural texture to the Banka Run Fest covered elsewhere in this research, which runs in the same broader province.

sections.heading: A Different Landscape Again
paragraphs: Where Ijen offers volcanic terrain and Minang offers canyon scenery, Belitung's geography is fundamentally different again -- an island historically shaped by mining and maritime trade rather than mountain geology. [1] That range across genuinely distinct Indonesian landscapes is the Geopark Run Series' core appeal, and this leg extends it further.

sections.heading: Details Still 'Coming Soon'
paragraphs: Both the exact venue and registration status are listed as still to be confirmed ('TBA' and 'Coming Soon' respectively) as of this writing. [1] Given the series' track record at its other three legs, specifics are likely to firm up well ahead of the 18 April 2027 race date.

sections.heading: Should You Run It?
paragraphs: If you're following the Geopark Run Series across its expanding roster of Indonesian islands and landscapes, the Belitong leg on 18 April 2027 extends that journey to a genuinely distinct tin-and-pepper island destination. Watch for venue and registration details to firm up closer to race day.
